title: Dynamic BH3 Profiling Protocol Adapted From Letai Lab
author: Dennis Juarez
materials: During the spin, prepare your 2x peptide solutions in MEB2- P25. The peptide stocks are made at 100x and should be diluted 1:50. Prepare enough for every cell line and treatment used in the assay. Minimum Total Volume= (#cell line x #treatment condition + 1)* 25 uL Note on panel: Always include in your peptide panel DMSO only, PUMA2A, and Alamethicin to act as controls for cytochrome C.
Permeabilized cells will appear blue under the microscope.

steps.title: Count and allocate cells
steps.instruction: Count cells and aliquot 2,000,000 cells per treatment condition into a 1.7 mL tube (the assay uses 200,000 cells for 8 peptides; cell concentration at exposure should be 0.5–4 ×10⁶ cells/mL, we use 2 ×10⁶ cells/mL). Scale up or down as needed.

steps.title: Spin cells down
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 500 × g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Optional surface marker staining
steps.instruction: If surface‑marker staining is required, block and stain the cells now, then spin down again before digitonin permeabilization. A fixable viability dye is recommended for samples with high death or variable viability; decide now and proceed to the fixation steps later.

steps.title: Wash cells with PBS
steps.instruction: Aspirate any media, resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL PBS, and spin down in a cold centrifuge to wash the cells.

steps.title: Test digitonin permeabilization
steps.instruction: Determine the lowest digitonin concentration that gives 100 % permeabilization:

substeps.instruction: Dilute digitonin stock to 0.016 % in MEB2‑P25 and perform five 2‑fold serial dilutions to obtain 0.008 %, 0.004 %, 0.002 %, 0.001 %, and 0.0005 % (each at 2× final).
Combine 5 µL of the cell suspension with 5 µL of each digitonin dilution.
Add 10 µL trypan blue, mix, and load onto a hemocytometer.
Identify the lowest concentration where all cells appear blue (100 % permeabilized).

steps.title: Select optimal digitonin concentration
steps.instruction: Choose the final digitonin concentration based on the test (the Letai guide suggests 0.001 % final, but use the lowest concentration from 0.008 % to 0.00025 % that yields complete permeabilization for your cells).

steps.title: Equilibrate MEB2-P25 buffer
steps.instruction: Allow the MEB2‑P25 buffer to reach room temperature (1–2 hours; preferably overnight) because BH3 profiling is temperature‑sensitive.

steps.title: Prepare digitonin working solution
steps.instruction: Dilute digitonin to 2× the chosen final concentration in MEB2‑P25 buffer; this solution will be used to resuspend the cells.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in digitonin solution
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in 250 µL of the diluted digitonin/MEB2‑P25 solution (enough for ten 25 µL peptide exposures, with extra volume).

steps.title: Prepare peptide master mixes
steps.instruction: Dilute each peptide in DMSO to 100× the desired final exposure concentration (e.g., BIM 0.001–100 µM, BID 0.01–100 µM, PUMA 0.1–100 µM, BAD 0.1–100 µM, NOXA 1–100 µM, HRK 1–100 µM, MS1 0.1–10 µM, FS1 0.1–10 µM, ABT199 0.1–1 µM, WEHI‑539 0.1–1 µM, A‑1331852 0.1–1 µM, A‑1155463 0.1–1 µM, S63845 1–10 µM). Store working dilutions at –20 °C for up to a week; fresh BH3 mimetics should be prepared immediately before use.

steps.title: Add peptide to plate wells
steps.instruction: In a V‑bottom 96‑well plate, dispense 25 µL of each 2× peptide solution into the bottom of the appropriate wells.

steps.title: Add cells to wells
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL of the cell suspension to each well, placing the droplet on the wall closest to you; gently tap the row after addition.

steps.title: Mix cells and peptide
steps.instruction: Mix the 25 µL cell and 25 µL peptide volumes by gently tapping the sides of the plate (or using a low‑speed plate vortexer, avoiding spillage).

steps.title: Incubate for peptide exposure
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature: typically 1 hour (30 min for highly sensitive cells, 1.5 hours for hardier lines). Adjust based on your cell line.

steps.title: Prepare Cytochrome C staining mix
steps.instruction: During incubation, dilute human Cytochrome C (BioLegend) 1:40 in 10× Cytochrome C Staining Buffer; prepare enough for 10 µL per well plus extra.

steps.title: Fix cells with PFA
steps.instruction: Add 16.5 µL of 8 % PFA to each well (final ≈2 % PFA); gently tap the row after addition. Use the freshest PFA available to prevent loss of Cytochrome C.

steps.title: Post‑fix incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Neutralize fixation
steps.instruction: Add 16.5 µL of N2 buffer to each well and gently tap the row.

steps.title: Add Cytochrome C stain
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of the 1:40 diluted Cytochrome C staining mix to each well; gently tap the row.

steps.title: Seal plate and incubate
steps.instruction: Seal the plate with a foil (or clear) seal if kept in the dark. Incubate 4 hours at room temperature (in a drawer) or overnight (≥16 hours) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Adjust volume with PBS
steps.instruction: Add approximately 50 µL PBS to each well to bring the total volume to ~150 µL.

steps.title: Acquire data on flow cytometer
steps.instruction: On the cytometer, open the BH3 Profile Template and Instrument Settings; set the FSC‑H threshold to exclude debris. Run a DMSO control to set the Cytochrome C‑high population above the second log, then run a BIM 10 µM control to ensure the Cytochrome C‑low population is below the second log. Acquire 125 µL per sample, collecting 10,000 events.
